notes: Account summary: Sailsync is a mid-market customer-success platform (SaaS) with a growing support KB. Evaluating hosted inference to replace an in-house elastic+custom reranker stack.
Workload profile: moderate indexing scale (~3M articles / 15-25M embeddings), high QPS at peak (target 800-1500 qps), bursty daytime traffic aligned to NA/EU support hours.
Performance targets: p95 latency for search+rerank < 200ms; target cold-start tail < 350ms; throughput goal 1k sustained qps for best-effort routes.
Cost sensitivity: finance cap on per-query cost; goal is <$0.003/query at 1k qps average with batching and caching. Wants concrete tradeoffs (quantization vs rerank quality).
Model preferences: lightweight embedding model (384-1024 dim) for recall; separate reranker (cross-encoder) for top-50 candidates. Prefer Redwood-hosted catalog but open to specific model shims.
Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to cheaper model variant during peak or region failover; tenancy must support tenant-based routing policies.
Security/Compliance: SSO (SAML) mandatory for console access; audit logs for production requests; KMS integration for keys; EU data residency for subset of customers.
POC status: 10k-doc embedding import completed (internal POC), reranker trial with 100k synthetic queries showed ~180ms median but p95 spikes to 420ms — next step is Redwood's batching/caching test.
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable unit economics and a reranking path that doesn't blow up tail latency.'
Internal notes: prioritize response on cost-model run; Arjun to lead tech test, Maya to loop in pricing; security kickoff scheduled 2025-10-18.
Linked artifacts: pricing deck + security FAQ in Drive; Fireflies call captures customer constraints (see linked_fireflies).
